answer_text:
# 🛜 How to Set Up a New Router for Wi-Fi Access

Here is a complete step-by-step guide to get your new router up and running:

---

## ✅ Step 1: Check Your Internet Connection First

Before anything else, verify your internet connection is working. Connect your computer directly to your modem using an Ethernet cable to confirm the connection is active.

---

## ✅ Step 2: Choose the Right Location for Your Router

Router placement is critical for optimal performance. The location impacts signal strength, internet speed, and overall coverage. Choose a central location in your home with no metal objects or appliances nearby, and ensure the router is elevated off the ground for better range.

Also, keep the router away from other electronics. Common culprits include microwaves, older cordless phones, and Bluetooth devices that can interfere with the 2.4 GHz band.

---

## ✅ Step 3: Connect the Hardware

Plug the power adapter into the router and connect it to an electrical outlet. Then connect your modem to the router's WAN or Internet port using the included Ethernet cable. Power on both the modem and router and wait for them to fully boot up.

> 💡 **Tip:** The WAN/Internet port on the router is usually a different color than the rest of the ports.

---

## ✅ Step 4: Connect Your Device to the Router

Connect your device to the router. Use an Ethernet cable to plug a wired device (desktop or laptop) into one of the router's LAN ports. Alternatively, use the router's supplied Wi-Fi login information to access the router using a computer, smartphone, or tablet.

---

## ✅ Step 5: Access the Router's Admin Panel

Open a web browser and enter the default IP address, which is usually `http://192.168.0.1`. Enter the default login credentials and start configuring the essential settings.

> 💡 **Tip:** To configure the router, you'll need to log in using its default admin name and password. You can usually find this information printed on the router itself or in an accompanying user manual.

---

## ✅ Step 6: Change Default Login Credentials

Once you're in, you should immediately create a new username and password. The defaults are usually something like "admin" and "password1234," which are not secure — so make sure to change them at the first opportunity.

---

## ✅ Step 7: Configure Your Wi-Fi Network (SSID & Password)

Change the SSID (network name), Wi-Fi password, and admin username and password to secure your network from the very start and ensure that your data and devices remain protected.

When choosing a name for your Wi-Fi, avoid personal details like your address or last name.

Customize your wireless network name and password for both the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands, then click Next when finished.

---

## ✅ Step 8: Select Your Internet Connection Type

Choose your internet connection type. The most common options are:
- **Dynamic/Automatic IP** – Use if your provider requires no credentials from you (typically selected by default).
- **PPPoE** – Use if your provider requires a username and password.
- **Static IP** – Use if your provider has assigned you a fixed IP address.

---

## ✅ Step 9: Update the Router's Firmware

Your router may need a firmware update. Update it as soon as possible, since new firmware might fix bugs or offer new security protections. Some routers may download new firmware automatically, but many do not — you may need to check for updates through the app or the browser interface.

---

## ✅ Step 10: Enable Security Settings

Turn on WPA3 or WPA2 security and disable open networks. Keep guest access separate if you use it.

> 💡 **Tip:** WPA3 is the newest and most secure protocol. If unavailable, use WPA2 with AES encryption.

---

## ✅ Step 11: Test Your Connection

After configuring all the settings, test your internet connection to ensure everything is working correctly. Access the internet through your Wi-Fi network and confirm the speeds are consistent. Testing the network helps you identify weak spots in coverage, network performance, and speed inconsistencies early on.

---

## 🔧 Optional Advanced Settings

Depending on your needs, you can customize additional features such as a **Guest Network**, **Quality of Service (QoS)**, **Parental Controls**, and **MAC Filtering**. Each has a specific function and can be enabled depending on your household's needs.

---

## 🚨 Troubleshooting Tips

- If the internet connection test fails, double-check that your Ethernet cable is fully seated in both the modem and the router's WAN port.
- If issues persist, restart the modem first, then the router. Check that all cables are plugged in correctly.
- If the setup wizard doesn't appear, clear your browser cache and try again. Confirm that your browser is Chrome, Firefox, or Edge, and that you typed the address into the address bar rather than a search bar.
